transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-29 14:00 PDT (45m)
Attendees: Eva Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Mariner - Head of ML), Priya Nair (Mariner - Infra), Jordan Lee (Mariner - Product)
Recording ID: ffx-20260329-6821

[00:00] Eva Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Eva from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Samir, our SE. Quick agenda: we want to walk through Optimize recommendations - batching, prefix/KV cache, and the cost model spreadsheet, then Q&A and next steps.

[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hey thanks, quick note we're on a bit tight timeline for Q2 pilot, so want to see concrete numbers and the impact on p95 for our card auth path.

[00:30] Samir Patel: totally, we'll focus on the ticketed path - small prompt sizes ~120 tokens avg, tail sensitive. I'll show how batching windows and KV prefix caching change cost per 1M requests and tail latencies.

[01:05] Priya Nair: quick interject — we're behind a VPC and have strict KMS requirements, also need to see audit logs.

[01:12] Eva Chen: noted, we'll attach SOC2 / KMS / audit docs after the call. Samir, do the demo.

[01:20] Samir Patel: alright jumping into the Optimize tab in the Console... (screen share noisy) so first thing: batching. Redwood supports adaptive batching with client-side hints and server-side windowing. For Mariner's workload, because avg seq len ~120 tokens, if you allow 20-50ms batching window we see 4-6x token throughput improvement but increases p95 by about 30-80ms depending on hardware and model size.

[02:05] Jordan Lee: ah can we see that in numbers? what's the dollars difference?

[02:10] Samir Patel: yep. Here's the cost model spreadsheet link (shared): https://redwood.internal/sheets/mariner-cost-model (note: placeholder). Example row: Hosted gpt-3-like open model sim: no cache, baseline cost $X per 1M tokens; with 40ms batching window we reduce per-token cost by ~42% but p95 increases from 110ms to 190ms in our synthetic. With KV prefix cache for repeated auth prompts, you can shave off ~60% of token compute for warm prefixes which pushes p95 back down and reduces cost further.

[03:00] Liam: the 'gpt-3-like open model sim' - is that Redwood-verified or synthetic? sometimes these sim numbers are optimistic.

[03:08] Samir: good call, it's a Redwood-verified profile on our test fleet, synthetic traces from your sample we requested earlier - but yeah, real infra will vary. That's why we recommend a short pilot benchmark.

[03:35] Priya: what's the difference between prefix cache and KV cache? we've read mixed docs.

[03:40] Samir: short answer: prefix cache (or prefix/KV cache nomenclature) - prefix cache stores repeated token prefixes in the KV cache so subsequent calls can skip early decoding compute; KV cache generally refers to LLM KV cache used during generation to avoid recomputing attention for earlier tokens. In Redwood's Optimize, we have a prefix-aware caching layer that recognizes repeated user/system prefixes across requests - so it's effectively a warm-spot cache for common prompts like auth templates.

[04:10] Jordan: so for our auth path, which is templated, sounds like a big win. How does that behave on dedicated vs hosted?

[04:18] Samir: on Hosted, we can enable shared prefix cache across multi-tenant nodes with strict isolation rules - it's safe but slightly more conservative cache TTLs. On Dedicated, cache locality is higher (same GPU pool) so cache hit rates and latencies improve, often doubling effective warm-hit benefit versus hosted for identical workloads. But Dedicated has committed cost.

[04:40] Liam: any numbers for warm-hit latencies? p95?

[04:45] Samir: warm hits tend to have token compute of effectively <5ms per token for the prefix portion since KV retrieval is O(1) in the runtime; network and decoding still apply. End-to-end p95 for a cached auth template in our tests moved from 190ms to ~120ms with caching+light batching. So you regain most of the tail improvement.

[05:15] Priya: interesting, but how do you account for cache churn and cold starts? our traffic has many small bursts and a long tail of infrequent merchants.

[05:27] Samir: yep churn matters. Our cost model includes hit-rate assumptions. We showed three scenarios: high-reuse (hit-rate 70%+), mixed (30-50%), and low reuse (<15%). For low reuse, KV cache doesn't help much and batching wins on unit cost but hurts latency. We also have an auto-eviction policy and customer-configurable TTLs; you can pin prefixes for critical paths.

[06:05] Liam: what about multi-region/regulatory data — can cache keys be stored only in-region?

[06:11] Eva Chen: yes, for Private/Dedicated we can enforce region-local cache and keys. We'll include the architecture note in the security doc.

[06:20] Samir: jumping back to the spreadsheet — here's an example cost calc: baseline tokens-per-request = 150, calls-per-second 2500 (burst), without caching cost = $Y per hour. With 40ms batching reduces tokens CPU cost by 45% and with KV cache warm-hit 60% of requests drop effective token compute for prefix, so net cost reduction ~65% for that segment. But again, these are model/hardware-specific.

[07:05] Jordan: you said 40ms window - how do you tune window vs latency SLOs?

[07:12] Samir: Redwood Optimize provides suggested window by SLO. You enter p95 target and throughput and we surface recommended batching window + expected cost delta. There's also an option for micro-batching on SE/GPU level where we prioritize low-latency buckets.

[07:35] Priya: do you support dynamic routing - like route premium requests to low-latency path and cheaper requests to batch-heavy path?

[07:41] Samir: yes that's core to the routing layer - per-route policies, weight-based fallbacks; you can tag routes as latency-critical and they'll hit a lower-batch-size pool or dedicated instances. We'll demo that in config if helpful.

[08:05] Liam: security question - how are cached items encrypted and who has access? prefix data sometimes contains PII (last 4 of card).

[08:15] Eva Chen: fair point. Redwood can configure mask rules to strip sensitive fields before caching; cached KV is encrypted at rest and in transit. For Private, keys can be your KMS/HSM. We will attach the KMS section in the security pack.

[08:40] Jordan: what's the impact on cost of masking/preprocessing versus caching? if we pre-hash or token-mask, do we reduce hit-rate?

[08:48] Samir: yes masking changes hit patterns; if you hash merchant id only, you'll maintain reuse, but if you remove too much context you might reduce cache utility. We recommend canonicalization that normalizes merchant names but keeps templating. We'll help with a sample canonicalization function.

[09:20] Liam: question about quantization - you mentioned earlier Redwood suggests quantized variants. How does quantization interact with batching/kv cache?

[09:28] Samir: good Q. Quantization reduces per-token compute cost but may slightly increase latency on some ops depending on kernel selection. KV cache still helps equally; in some hardware combos, quantized models + batching give the best cost/perf. But there are quality tradeoffs; Optimize includes quality/regression checks to ensure evals pass thresholds when switching quantized models.

[10:05] Priya: can we see a real run with our sample traces?

[10:10] Samir: we didn't run the full benchmark before this call but we can run a quick micro-benchmark with a subset — Eve sorry Samir — (laughter) — I'll trigger the run after this. Ideally we get your sample traces and run overnight.

[10:30] Eva Chen: attaching the ask: please upload 24-48 hours of p95/p99 traces and a small sample of prompts (anonymized) to the shared S3 folder link we'll send. That's what Samir needs for accurate numbers.

[10:55] Jordan: timeline - if we share traces today, how long for the benchmark?

[11:00] Samir: typical turnaround 3-5 business days for a focused benchmark, faster if we prioritize. We'll scope the exact run in the follow-up sheet.

[11:20] Liam: ok next, license/pricing - if we go Dedicated, how do commit levels change per-token pricing?

[11:28] Eva Chen: Dedicated has reserved capacity discounts; the cost model worksheet shows committed vs on-demand delta. Example: reserved reduces unit compute by ~30-40% in our examples, but requires commit. We'll include illustrative rows in the spreadsheet.

[11:50] Priya: are there any known issues with cold-cache storms if we scale new nodes quickly?

[11:58] Samir: cold-starts can cause a spike; we mitigate with pre-warming and warm-up policies. Also we have smart hashing to avoid simultaneous evictions and staggered rehydration. For large scale-ups we recommend a fast-warm policy.

[12:20] Jordan: can we pin critical prefixes to stay resident?

[12:24] Samir: yes, prefix pinning for critical routes is available on Dedicated and on Private with config; hosted has a managed version. Pinning will increase memory footprint but preserves hit-rate.

[12:45] Liam: fine, last thing - can you share a sample pilot proposal?

[12:50] Eva Chen: we'll send a 30-day pilot plan: ingest traces, run bench, configure caching + batching, run A/B on cost/quality, deliver report + recommended config. We aim to have the pilot run in April if Mariner approves.

[13:15] Priya: please include our security team in follow-up and send SOC2 + KMS docs.

[13:22] Eva Chen: will do.

[13:30] (brief cross talk, logistics)

[13:50] Samir: quick clarifying point - when you saw 'KV cache', if you ever see 'prefix cache' in docs it's the same feature set in Optimize, naming sometimes inconsistent in older docs, apologies for confusion.

[14:10] Jordan: noted, thanks.

[14:20] Eva Chen: recap of next steps — Eva send cost model + security docs; Samir run bench after Mariner provides traces; Mariner provide traffic profile; schedule pilot kickoff. Any final Qs?

[14:40] Liam: no, thanks all. Looking forward to the spreadsheet.

[14:45] Eva Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the sheet. End call.
